events.summary: 20S & 30S FULL MOON HIKE AT MT WACHUSETT

description.plain:
Wednesday, August 26, 2026 | 6:30 PM
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001GLkf2AG/
Join other 20s and 30s for an evening hike up Mt. Wachusett during a (almost) full moon. We will hike 3-4 miles with a total elevation gain of about 750 ft. Weather permitting, we plan to spenda few minutes at the summit to enjoy the sunset and moonrise. The trails will include sections of moderate terrain and we will be moving at a moderate pace. Proper equipment will be required for this hike, including: hiking and weather appropriate clothing, water, and a headlamp.

events.summary: Flags on the 48 - A September 11 Memorial Hike: South Kinsman

description.plain:
Saturday, September 12, 2026
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001FKlp2AG/
We are organizing a team for the Flags on the 48 memorial event. Join our Chapter in honoring those who died on Sept 11 by helping to raise our flag over South Kinsman. Out and back hike via the Lonesome Lake, Fishin' Jimmy and Mt. Kinsman trails, 10 mi., ~ 3,200' elevation gain, with average, strenuous, and very strenuous terrain, at a slower-moderate pace (1-2 mph). Limited to 12, including the leaders, physically fit hikers with current, i.e., within the past year, upcountry hiking experience. All participants will be screened for this hike to ensure we can stay together as a group; otherwise, it can create an unsafe situation.This is a full day event with an early start. Leave room in your pack to carry group gear: flag, PVC pipe used to construct the flagpole, guy lines and other hardware for securing the pole. We will arrive at the peak to allow time to set up/secure the flagpole at the summit and raise the flag before 12 noon. The flag then flies from noon through 2 pm. We then will lower the flag, deconstruct the flag pole,guy lines, etc. and pack up our gear.Required gear:• Bring what you need to stay warm, dry, and happy for an extended day on the summit• A pack large enough to hold all your gear + group gear• 3-4 liters of water• Snacks and trail lunch• Pad to sit on• Sunscreen• Bug repellent• Headlamp• Rain gear• Layers to add & subtract to regulate your body temperature throughout the day, including, and not limited to, a puffy jacket, winter hat/mittens/gloves

description.plain:
Friday, September 25, 2026 | 5:00 PM
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001FiWP2A0/
Hear ye! Hear ye! Embraceth adventure and occasions of socialization most joyous!WE'RE GOING TO THE RENAISSANCE FESTIVAL, PEASANTS!!! WOOOO-ETH!!!Join your fellow 20s & 30s for a Ren-Fest camp out the weekend of September 25-27. We have a group campsite reserved at Myles Standish State Forest for camping Friday and Saturday night thus enabling easy access to King Richard's Faire in Carver, MA on Saturday, September 26!20s & 30s folx from any chapter are welcome to join us on this jaunt, fealty to the Worcester Chapter is not a pre-requisite. Camping will be capped at 20 people (campsite regulation) but for anyone unable to join us for camping, all are still welcome to come meet up with us at King Richard's Faire for a day of festivities.Several items of note:Members of the Jackalope Society will be given one week registration preference (August 30 - September 5), after that it'll be first come first serve to register.If you're looking to just camp but not Ren-Fest, this event is not for you and we recommend looking for tenting elsewhere. Come ready to revel renaissance style.You must secure your own ticket to King Richard's Faire! It can sell out, so we recommend getting that ticket as soon as you're confirmed for this camp out (www.kingrichardsfaire.net). Tickets are $40 for September 26.No meals will be provided on this camping trip, however the Worcester Gear Shed can provide camp equipment. Cost for the campsite is pay what you can ($5 is appreciated).Costumes for the King Richard's Faire are encouraged but not required! If you'd like to borrow or need some tips, your fearless leader is a massive nerd and can offer budget friendly recommendations.

Friday, October 2, 2026 | 4:00 PM
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001GWZd2AO/
Shovels and mattocks and axes, oh my! Do you hear the call? It's trail work time! Your fellow 20s & 30s are ready to get down and dirty, are you ready to join?Two nights and two days at the Camp Dodge Trails Center in Gorham, NH, in the heart of the White Mountains. Under the instruction of staff from the AMC Trails Department we'll lend our time and hands to bolstering the good work done by AMC Pro Crews all over the region. In years past we've installed bog bridges, done rock work, installed boardwalks, and more! The work is vigorous but good for the soul and amazing to see results that will pay off for decades to come.This trip includes 2 nights (Friday and Saturday) stay in one of the shared bunkhouses at Camp Dodge (we'll have one to our group, but we will be sharing) and delicious dinner Friday and Saturday + breakfast & lunch Saturday and Sunday (dietary needs will be met). Each day we'll rally after breakfast, go through the plan for the day, load ourselves and our gear up, and then off to the worksite. We'll put in a full day on Saturday and a partial day on Sunday so we all have a chance to head home.This trip is intended for people in their 20s & 30s with an interest in trail work, conservation, and preserving the outdoors we know and love. No trail work experience is required, but is always welcome! All you need is a desire to learn and the ability to meet a minimum physical threshold. Work each day will involve hiking a few miles while carrying your pack, tools, and any necessary supplies over varied terrain with a moderate elevation gain. It's good work but it can be hard work. Prepare to be sore and tired but filled with the warm glow of knowing your contributions matter!At the end of our work days, we'll be relaxing and socializing around Camp Dodge. There's nothing like a day digging in the dirt to make fast friends with your fellow crewmates!This trip costs $50. Your fee goes directly to the cost of food at the Camp Dodge kitchen.If you have any questions at all, please let your leaders know! We're happy to provide more information and to hopefully see you out there!

Friday, October 9, 2026 | 12:00 PM
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001D6F72AK/
 You are cordially invited to join the Worcester Chapter for our 33rd anniversary trip to Western Maine to enjoy the gorgeous autumn colors of Maine over Columbus Day weekend. We'll be staying at the Maine House, located on the shore of beautiful Lake Christopher in the village of Bryant Pond. The charming historic house will be the base for our many hikes and other outdoor activities. The Maine House has cozy private rooms for couples and comfy bunks for singles. The dining area has a panoramic view over the lake, and a large living room with a fireplace invites all to relax and socialize during the evening. In addition, there is a hot tub and a steam room to help you recover after your day of activities. Paddle right out the door on Lake Christopher in canoes provided by the house. The trip fee includes three nights lodging (Fri - Sun), three breakfasts and make-your-own-lunch buffets, and two tasty dinners. Everyone helps with set-up or clean-up for a meal. With about 30 people on the trip, we will be able to offer various levels of hikes each day, ranging from easy to strenuous, as well as other activities. We will lead one road biking trip, and there are nearby DIY paddling opportunities. The trip cost this year is $175. Join us for this Worcester Chapter classic which draws participants from all over the club.
